## The problem with block maxima

```{julia}
#| echo: false
nh_annmax = AnnMaxRecord(nh; detrend=:none, units=u"m")
fig = Figure(; size=(800, 300))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="Year", ylabel="Annual max (m above MSL)")
scatter!(ax, obsyears(nh_annmax), nh_annmax.levels; color=colors[1], markersize=8)
fig
```

New Haven, CT (NOAA 8465705).
Sandy (2012) and Irene (2011) tower over everything else.
Do we have 26 annual maxima, or 2 real extremes and 24 ordinary high tides?

## Same story, different coast

```{julia}
#| echo: false
gv_annmax = AnnMaxRecord(gv; detrend=:none, units=u"m")
fig = Figure(; size=(800, 300))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="Year", ylabel="Annual max (m above MSL)")
scatter!(ax, obsyears(gv_annmax), gv_annmax.levels; color=colors[2], markersize=8)
fig
```

Galveston Pier 21 (NOAA 8771450), 120 years of hourly data.
Ike (2008, 3.0 m) and Carla (1961, 2.3 m) stand apart; everything else is under 1.4 m.
Block maxima treats the year with Ike and a quiet year the same way: one observation each.

## Why peaks over threshold?

Block maxima is **statistically wasteful** (Coles, §4.1).
It reduces a year of sub-annual data to one number.

The HEC fishing analogy: block maxima keeps only the biggest fish each day.
Peaks over threshold keeps every fish above the legal length.

Peaks over threshold uses **more of the data**, which means tighter confidence intervals on the same return level.
The threshold is a modeling choice you can **diagnose** (mean residual life plot, parameter stability).
"One year" is a convention nobody checks.

We need two ingredients:

1. **The distribution of exceedances** above the threshold (the GPD)
2. **How often exceedances happen** (a rate, events per year)

## What the hourly record looks like

```{julia}
#| echo: false
gv_times = [r.time for r in gv]
gv_levels = [ustrip(uconvert(u"m", r.level)) for r in gv]
i_start = findfirst(t -> year(t) == 2008 && month(t) == 8, gv_times)
i_end = findlast(t -> year(t) == 2008 && month(t) == 10, gv_times)
t_sub = gv_times[i_start:i_end]
l_sub = gv_levels[i_start:i_end]

fig = Figure(; size=(800, 300))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="Date", ylabel="Water level (m)")
lines!(ax, eachindex(t_sub), l_sub; color=colors[2], linewidth=0.5)
hlines!(ax, [0.6]; color=:red, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
ax.xticks = (
    [findfirst(t -> day(t) == 1, t_sub[i:end]) + i - 1 for i in 1:length(t_sub) if i == 1 || (month(t_sub[i]) != month(t_sub[i-1]))][1:3],
    ["Aug", "Sep", "Oct"],
)
fig
```

Galveston, Aug--Oct 2008.
The dashed line is a candidate threshold.
Ike keeps the gauge above it for days: those are not independent exceedances.
